summary.intent: Decide whether to avoid the JSON boundary in the tsrs checker by dispatching directly, then (after the prototype showed little gain) find out where the ~6.5 CPU-seconds of a cold default shadcn run actually go.
summary.outcome: A direct-dispatch spike (`spike/direct-dispatch`) proved byte-identical but saved only ~2-4% CPU, which overturned the earlier claim that the codec was 21% of busy time. The handoff and memory were corrected. A fresh PID-based profile (thread breakdown, rayon thread-count sweep, user/sys split) was started but no result was reported.

repo: `CheckerHost` has nine methods; six can be built from `pub` tsrs API (`context`, `snapshot`, `node_handle`, `source_file_descriptor`, `_matches`, `source_file_node_id`). `acquire_cached_source_file` and `clone_snapshot_with_auto_imports` need private session state and can't be built externally.

A direct-dispatch prototype would add three dependencies pinned at =0.24.0 (`tsrs_ast`, `tsrs_compiler`, `tsrs_project`). It would also rely on serde_json's private `RawValue` token and skip tsrs's strict request validation.
`tsrs_core::json::Value` has no serde support, so the prototype needed a ~120-line custom `Deserializer`.
On current main the JSON codec is 2.0-4.5% of busy samples on shadcn (0.6-0.9% in tree mode), not 21%. Chakra shows no measurable difference.
Everything caliper uses is a checker-lane method except `createSnapshot`, `updateSnapshot`, `release`, `getSemanticDiagnostics`, `parseConfigFile` and `batchRequests`.
The `lint` recipe in `just` needs registry.npmjs.org access.

code.finding: New file holding `CaliperHost`, a `catch_unwind`-wrapped dispatch and the Value decoder. Top-level `getPropertiesOfType` (1,708 calls on shadcn) and `getTypesOfSymbols` (2,719) are routed through it.
Gained a tree payload alongside the text one so calls still run on the 512 MiB lanes. `CALIPER_SPIKE_TEXT=1` switches back to the text path.

workflow: macOS `sample` matches process names by substring, so it can attach to another session's process (e.g. `caliper-docgen-prof`). Profile by PID with a uniquely named binary.
Benchmarks on a loaded machine (load 40-130) need interleaved runs, paired differences and discarding degraded runs before drawing conclusions.
Verify a profiling number from a handoff before building on it. A wrong 21% figure drove a speculative rewrite and the user's frustration.
Subagent reports are not user authority. Correct any stale briefing and memory copies when a report overturns an earlier claim.

friction: The earlier profile likely attached to the wrong process, so the 21% codec claim was wrong and led to wasted prototype work.
Heavy machine load (40-130) made CPU measurements noisy. Five runs were degraded and excluded.
The user is frustrated that a cold run costs so many CPU seconds and that the explanation given earlier was wrong.
open_items: Find where the ~6.5 CPU-seconds of a cold shadcn run actually go. The PID-based profile, rayon thread sweep and user/sys breakdown were run but results not yet reported.
